new_findings.title: A single Delete keystroke in an empty paragraph before the Contents block permanently destroys the whole non-editable table of contents
new_findings.repro: 1) Create h1 'Top Title' + more headings; References → Contents (TOC inserted). 2) Caret at end of the h1 text; press Enter (creates empty block BEFORE the TOC). 3) Press Delete once. Observed: empty block AND the entire .np3-toc (contenteditable=false) Contents block vanish. Update-contents cannot repair (nothing left); recovery only via re-inserting Contents.
new_findings.expected: non-editable protected TOC survives ordinary Delete keystrokes (native contenteditable preserves a following contenteditable=false block)
controls: Native control (about:blank bare contenteditable, same structure): Delete → both blocks intact, non-editable div survives
In-app Backspace control: empty block adjacent to TOC + Backspace → TOC intact (asymmetry isolates forward-delete path)
new_findings.source_mechanism: no dedicated Delete interceptor found for this case (only Images/Ink intercept Delete); damage occurs through the app's post-edit paragraph normalization (preciseParagraph/withMutation/normalizeDom chain, app-js.txt ~line 4790+ writerActions) which merges/removes the empty block together with the following non-editable .np3-toc block; several guards exclude .np3-toc (tree walker filters, updateToc) but the delete/merge normalization path does not
new_findings.impact: silent loss of the generated Contents block from one keystroke; user must re-insert and re-anchor; headings survive so damage is contained to the TOC. Fix direction: guard forward-delete merge when next top-level block is .np3-toc/.np3-fndef/contenteditable=false (skip over it like the tree-walker guards do).
